category: scene release database (metadata and NFO, no download links)

free_tier.stated: The release lists are readable without an account; the JSON API at api.xrel.to answered a page reader with HTTP 403 and a 5-word bot challenge instead of content.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: release metadata, not an object

retention.stated: records persist; the release lists carry dated entries per category (console, TV, movies), newest first

egress.terms: no byte allowance: the site serves NFO text, screenshots and metadata, not files

interface_detail: A documented JSON API under api.xrel.to/v2/ (the v2 index path returned 404 from nginx, and /v2/ returned a 403 challenge), plus HTML release lists per category.
tooling: HTTP client for the API when the challenge permits; otherwise HTML scraping of the release lists. Nothing to download, so no rclone or debrid tool applies.
chaining: Use it as the metadata layer: given a release name from a DDL index, xREL gives the group, the date, the NFO and the IMDb/TVDB id, which is what makes a release name resolvable to a title.

limits.value: no published limit on the pages read; the API returned a 403 bot challenge to a page reader before any rate could be observed

limits_note: The challenge is the first obstacle, not a quota: the reader saw 'bot challenge' with a 5-word body at HTTP 403.
binding_note: An API challenge is not one of the seven constraints and no byte quota exists; a user meets the challenge first and would then meet an unpublished rate.

identity_cost.detail: The HTML lists were readable without an account. The API's authentication requirement was not established beyond the 403 challenge.

reliability_note: Cloudflare-style bot screening sits in front of the API, so a client that works today can be challenged tomorrow; the HTML surface answered normally.
confidence_note: The home page was read on 2026-10-23 and the API challenge was captured.

evidence.proved: live German scene release database, title 'xREL.v3 - Release & NFO Source #1', release lists with NFO links and sizes
HTTP 403 with a 5-word body: the reader classified it as a bot challenge, so no API content was read
HTTP 404 from nginx, so that documentation path does not exist
